messages:
lee: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on canary when KV hit ~92% of headroom. Batches forming with long prefixes pushed kernel route to fallback and we saw an OOM spike. Profiling attached.

sam: can you paste the profiler snippet? rough numbers are fine

lee: ```
perf: kernel_select=attn_fused_fast -> attn_generic
batch_size_avg=9 -> 5
token_budget_target=2048 -> 1024
kv_used=78GB/84GB (92%)
OOMs: 7 in 10m
```

priya: ack. Sounds like our batch admission is too eager on token budget when kv headroom is low. Proposed: implement a "mini-queue" admission that caps per-request token admit to 256 when kv_headroom < 15% and prefers small-batch kernel routes. Thoughts?

matt: +1. Also we should prefer a kernel route that keeps KV pinned (no aggressive prefetch). We saw `attn_fused_fast` allocate large temp buffers.

lee: exactly. I think three levers: 1) admission cap fallback (256 tokens) 2) queue prioritization to favor short-seq jobs 3) kernel route hint to avoid fused kernels when kv_headroom < X.

sam: agree. Can we land it as a runtime flag gated behind `runtime/kv-oom-experiments`? We'll need metrics: per-host OOM count, p99 latency, tokens/s.

priya: I'll sketch the feature flag: `--kv-admit-strategy=graceful-miniq` with params `min_headroom_pct=15, token_admit_cap=256, short_seq_bias=0.7`. We'll make defaults conservative.

matt: quick perf estimate from local: with cap 256 and miniq we regain headroom and drop OOMs to 0 in smoke runs, p99 latency +8-12% but tail stable.

lee: nice. Can we run a 10% canary on dedicated cluster `ded-rt-3`? Also add a perf regression check that blocks rollouts if tail latency +20%.

ops-bot: deploy created: canary/kv-miniq/4281234567 by priya — target ded-rt-3 10% — status: scheduled

sam: prioritize telemetry: `kv_headroom_pct`, `batch_route`, `kernel_route`, `oom_count`, `token_admit` — add to trace spans.

priya: will open PR tomorrow with feature flag and unit tests. Putting an RFC in #eng-runtime-next-day for review.

lee: thanks. if anyone has quick objections call them out now — otherwise we'll land the flag and run canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

matt: none from me. +1

priya: note: also added a small change to admission sampler to prefer nodes with lower kv pressure for larger batches — avoids oscillation.

lee: perfect. tagging @oncall for visibility. @oncall can you monitor the canary and escalate if OOMs spike?

oncall: got it — will watch logs/alerts and post summary at 09:30 UTC
